page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a virtual server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the system contains 32 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz with multithreading enabled at two threads per core. The processor configuration includes a 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The instance achieves top 10% placement in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as Passmark CPU and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read and write operations scoring in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates strong performance in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and LLM inference processing for small to medium models, though large 70B model inference is unsupported due to the absence of a dedicated GPU.

A primary architectural tradeoff of this instance is its storage configuration, which relies on 1 GB of network-attached storage rather than high-capacity local NVMe drives. This makes it highly dependent on external network storage for data-intensive operations. However, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose enterprise workloads. Given its high-tier CPU performance and substantial memory capacity, this server is well-suited for software compilation, database operations, text and image processing, and medium-scale web serving.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 32 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, this instance delivers top-tier performance in CPU-intensive benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and software compilation tests. It features advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. A key architectural tradeoff is its reliance on 1 GB of network storage rather than local NVMe drives, and it lacks a dedicated GPU. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is optimized for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, image processing, and medium-scale web serving.
